waiting.title: 9397 snowplough: two corrections to the plough’s lift, and two parts for function 1
waiting.what: Two things for the 9397, one item. (a) A correction to the published file. The plough hangs on a double parallelogram: a grey 5-long link joins the middle hole of one yellow arm to the middle hole of the other, and both arms pivot on one frame beam two holes apart, so the link lies parallel to that beam (booklet step 37). In the file the link is tipped 0.09 degrees and its pin is drawn 0.10 LDU off its hole. The two loops then disagree, and the plough’s drive locks after a hair’s turn. The correction makes the link level and puts the pin in its hole. (b) A change to the list you signed. Function 1, the motor and gearbox, was signed with no parts to watch. It now names the two ring shafts that turn whenever the motor runs (p157 and p160).
waiting.effect: Function 3, the plough, goes from partly working to working, and its motion comes back to its start. The set then has all six functions working, and the count goes from 742 to 743. Function 1 still works, now with something to watch.
waiting.confidence: High. The parallelogram follows from the hole spacing the booklet shows. Claude ran it in the viewer with the correction switched on and the collision pass ready: with the plough’s lever set, the motor raises the plough evenly, 0.21 LDU a step for six steps, and the tipping frame and the truck stay. Without the correction the plough moves 0.4 LDU and the motor stops. The worker saw the same, and the plough come back.

coming.title: The next offer of main
coming.what: preview has 742 working functions and main 701, but Claude does not offer main yet. A measurement on 18 November showed how far the check and the viewer differ: in the viewer a collision between parts stops 694 motions in 330 working or partly working functions before the check’s turn ends, and in 205 working functions every stopped motion stops before half way. Many of these are real ends of travel; some are parts that are designed to touch. Two steps come first: the viewer and the check tell the designed contacts apart by where the parts meet, and the check then makes the viewer’s stop. The count of working functions may change a good deal with that. Then a full check and a slow check of the 8110 on the commit offered. Also still out of the count by a hand-set result: the 41999’s function 7.
